newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Blue chip gains drive Slovak BSE to year-high.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip gains drive Slovak BSE to year-high.

text.p: 1540 GMT - Slovak blue chips close mostly higher in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Friday, driving the SAX index to a year high.
* Slovnaft up 15 crowns at 870, VSZ up 10 at 695, VUB Bank up 25 at 1,725 crowns, Slovakofarma up 145 at 4,700 crowns.
Slovak blue chips closed mostly higher in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Friday, driving the SAX index up 1.87 points to a year-high of 196.67.
Drug producer Slovakofarma, the fourth largest issue on the 16-share index, led the drive higher, gaining 145 crowns, or 3.2 percent, to close at 4,700.
Oil refiner Slovnaft gained 15 crowns to close at 870, while steel maker VSZ rose 10 crowns to 695 and commercial bank VUB VSEO.BV closed up 25 crowns at 1,725.
Brokers said they expect stronger foreign and domestic interest in the coming weeks, which should help the bourse maintain its current bullish sentiment in near future.
Bohus Betko of ING Barings said domestic and foreign demand could help Slovnaft extend its uptrend, and that VSZ should also continue to firm.

"The offer to sell Slovnaft is now lower, but I think the share may rise to around 875 crowns next week. This might be the starting point for future trades, but the further trend will only depend on the demand side, which is hard to predict at the moment," he said.
Brokers noted that low volumes in Slovakofarma indicated the price was being pushed up artficially in order to place larger packages of shares on the market at higher levels.
Overall volume fell to 276,291 shares, from 365,153 stocks traded on Thursday, while the turnover rose to 352.38 million crowns, from 177.34 million.
